ABSTRACT                                                                                     KEYWORDS
Simple graph algorithms such as PageRank have been the target of                             Graph Mining, Graph Pattern Matching, Graph Learning, Clique
numerous hardware accelerators. Yet, there also exist much more                              Mining, Clique Listing, Clique Enumeration, Subgraph Isomor-
complex graph mining algorithms for problems such as clustering                              phism, Parallel Graph Algorithms, Processing In Memory, Process-
or maximal clique listing. These algorithms are memory-bound                                 ing Near Memory, Graph Accelerators, Instruction Set Architecture
and thus could be accelerated by hardware techniques such as
Processing-in-Memory (PIM). However, they also come with non-                                ACM Reference Format:
straightforward parallelism and complicated memory access pat-                               Maciej Besta1 , Raghavendra Kanakagiri2 , Grzegorz Kwasniewski1 , Rachata

terns. In this work, we address this problem with a simple yet

use PIM to accelerate SISA instructions. The key design idea is to
alleviate the bandwidth needs of SISA instructions by mapping set
operations to two types of PIM: in-DRAM bulk bitwise computing                               1    INTRODUCTION
for bitvectors representing high-degree vertices, and near-memory                            Research on graph analytics in computer architecture has mostly
logic layers for integer arrays representing low-degree vertices.                            targeted graph algorithms based on vertex-centric formulations [6,
Set-centric SISA-enhanced algorithms are efficient and outperform                            7, 12, 22, 65, 88, 113, 120, 142, 177, 183]. Some works also focus
hand-tuned baselines, offering more than 10× speedup over the                                on edge-centric or linear algebra paradigms [90, 134, 149, 151].
established Bron-Kerbosch algorithm for listing maximal cliques.                             Such algorithms have complexities described by low-degree poly-
We deliver more than 10 SISA set-centric algorithm formulations,                             nomials [91], e.g., O(n + m) for Breadth-First Search (BFS) [42] and
illustrating SISA’s wide applicability.                                                      O(m · #iterations) for iteration-based PageRank (PR) [21], where n
                                                                                             and m are numbers of vertices and edges, respectively.
